user_prompt: What's a good beginner-friendly resistance training plan? I can train 3 times a week.
ai_response:
A simple **full-body routine 3 days per week** is one of the best ways to build strength and muscle as a beginner. It gives you frequent practice with the main movement patterns while allowing plenty of recovery.

### Weekly schedule

- **Monday:** Workout A
- **Wednesday:** Workout B
- **Friday:** Workout A
- The following week: **B / A / B**, then repeat.

### Workout A

| Exercise | Sets × Reps |
| --- | --- |
| Squat (goblet squat or barbell squat) | 3 × 6–10 |
| Bench press or push-ups | 3 × 6–10 |
| Seated cable row or dumbbell row | 3 × 8–12 |
| Romanian deadlift | 2–3 × 8–10 |
| Plank | 3 × 20–45 sec |

### Workout B

| Exercise | Sets × Reps |
| --- | --- |
| Deadlift (or trap-bar deadlift) | 3 × 5–8 |
| Overhead press (dumbbells or barbell) | 3 × 6–10 |
| Lat pulldown or assisted pull-up | 3 × 8–12 |
| Split squat or walking lunge | 2–3 × 8–10 per leg |
| Side plank or dead bug | 3 sets |

### How hard to work

- Choose a weight that leaves you with about **1–3 reps in reserve** (you could do 1–3 more reps if you had to).
- Rest **1–2 minutes** between most sets, and **2–3 minutes** for heavier compound lifts like squats and deadlifts.

### Progression

When you can complete all your sets at the **top of the rep range** with good form:

- Increase the weight by the smallest available amount (typically 2.5–5%).
- Start again at the lower end of the rep range and build back up.

Example:

- Week 1: 3 × 8 at 20 kg
- Week 2: 3 × 10 at 20 kg
- Week 3: Increase to 22.5 kg and do 3 × 8

### Warm-up (5–10 minutes)

- 3–5 minutes of light cardio (walking, cycling, rowing)
- Dynamic movements for hips, shoulders, and ankles
- 1–3 lighter warm-up sets before your first heavy exercise

### A few tips

- Prioritize good technique over lifting heavier.
- Aim for **7–9 hours of sleep** most nights.
- Eat enough protein (around **1.2–1.6 g per kg of body weight per day** is a solid target for most beginners).
- Track your workouts so you can see your progress.

If you have access to a gym, this plan should take about **45–60 minutes** per session.

If you're training **at home** with only dumbbells or resistance bands, I can adapt this plan using the equipment you have.
